CIVIL SERVICE RULES AND REGULATIONS
   Effective as Revised - January 1, 1990, and June 2, 2011, with amendments
indicated by ordinance histories following the section amended
CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION
RULE I
ORGANIZATION AND OFFICIAL STAFF
Section 1
   The officers of the Commission shall consist of three members, qualified
electors of the City, not holding any other Municipal office, to be appointed
by the Mayor for a term of six years. An open position occurring during the
term of any member of the Civil Service Commission shall be filled for the
unexpired term in the manner authorized for an original appointment.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 2
   The Secretary to the Civil Service Commission is appointed by the Mayor and
shall supervise its office and have charge of preparation of examination papers
and schedules, the holding of examinations, the certification of eligibles, the
keeping of records, and the preparation of regulations prescribing the detailed
procedure to be followed in the administration of these rules and in carrying
out the routine business of the Commission. The Secretary of the Commission
shall keep official records in the form of minutes of all proceedings of the
Commission and will perform all such other duties as may be required by the
Commission. The Secretary shall maintain official records of the acts of the
Commission and shall oversee the maintenance, filing and preservation of all
records, papers and other data belonging to the Commission.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 3
   The regular meetings of the Commission shall be held at the City Hall on the
second Tuesday of the month at 5:00 p.m. Special meetings shall be held at the
City Hall by the Commission upon call by the Chairman or by the other two
members of the Commission. A majority of the Commission shall constitute a
quorum for the transaction of business at any special or regular meetings.
(Ord. 1996-19. Passed 3-25-96; Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 4
   The members of the Commission shall at the beginning of each year elect a
Chairman who shall preside at all meetings and other functions of the
Commission and shall serve for a term of one year. The Chairman shall sign with
the Secretary all documents, minutes and reports pertaining to the affairs of
the Commission. In the absence of the Chairman, a member shall perform the
duties of the Chairman.
Section 5
   The Civil Service Commission shall provide by rule for the ascertainment of
merit and fitness as the basis for appointment and promotion in the service of
the City as required by the Constitution of Ohio. Civil service examination
shall not be required for the appointment of any member of a board or
commission, or any head of a department other than the Police Department or
Fire Department, or any assistant to the Director of Law or to the Director of
Finance, or any secretary to the Mayor or to the head of any department, or for
appointment to any other office or position requiring peculiar and exceptional
qualifications. Any person who shall have served the City for at least one year
next preceding the taking effect of this Charter may be retained in the same or
any similar position without examination. Except as herein provided, the Civil
Service Commission shall determine the practicability of competitive
examinations for any nonelective office or job classification in the service of
the City.
RULE II
POSITIONS CLASSIFIED
Section 1
   The classified service of the City of Mayfield Heights shall include all
members of the Police and Fire Departments who have taken competitive
examinations for original appointments to said Departments.
Section 2
   The classes of positions as named and described in specifications adopted by
the Commission and with such amendments as may be made thereto under these
Rules and Regulations from time to time, and interpreted therein, shall
constitute the "Classification Plan" for the classification of positions in the
service of the City of Mayfield Heights.
Section 3
   Every position in the service existing when these Rules and Regulations take
effect or hereafter created shall be classified under the Classification Plan
by allocating it to its appropriate class. Such allocations shall be made by
the Civil Service Commission. Whenever a position shall have been allocated to
its appropriate class in the manner agreed to, the title of such class shall
forthwith become the title of such position in all administrative and
employment processes and documents.
Section 4
   Whenever a new position is established or the duties of a position are so
changed that, in effect, the old position as described by the specifications of
the class to which it was originally allocated no longer exists but in its
place there is created a position of a different class, the appointing officer
shall report such fact to the Civil Service Commission and transmit a full
statement of the circumstances and description of the duties. The Civil Service
Commission shall thereupon make investigation of the actual and proposed
duties, responsibilities and qualification requirements, and classify or
reclassify the position by allocating it to its appropriate class in accordance
with the Classification Plan in effect.
   The Civil Service Commission shall likewise, from time to time of its own
motion, make investigation of all positions in the service, and propose changes
in classification wherever the facts are considered to warrant such action.
Classification or reclassification in all such cases shall take effect
immediately upon approval by the Civil Service Commission.
Section 5
   Where a position has been reclassified by the Commission on account of
additional duties and responsibilities or to correct original errors in
classifications, the incumbent of the former position may be promoted or
appointed to the new position without examination upon request of the Mayor. It
must be shown to the satisfaction of the Commission that the person for whom
such promotion or appointment is requested has fully performed the additional
duties and assumed the responsibilities on account of which reclassification
was allowed and is fully qualified to fill the position.
Section 6
   The Civil Service Commission may, whenever circumstances warrant, amend the
specifications or characteristics for any class, and abolish, merge or divide
existing classes, or create new classes under the Classification Plan.
Section 7
   The specifications of classes of positions in the Classification Plan are
hereby declared to have the following force, effect and intertwinement:
   A.    They are descriptive only and not restrictive. They are intended to
indicate the kinds of positions that should be classified under the respective
classes, as determined by their duties, responsibilities, and qualification
requirements. Every factor essential for the proper performance of the duties
of a position shall be considered in assigning such position in its proper
class.
   B.    In determining the class to which any position should be allocated,
the specifications of each class shall be considered as a whole. Consideration
is to be given to the general duties, typical tasks, responsibilities,
desirable entrance qualifications and relationships to other classes in
determining the class into which a position shall be assigned.
   C.    As to the particular parts of the determining factors and
specifications of classes, the following principals of interpretation shall
apply:
      1.    The "Duties Statement" shall be construed as a general description
of the kind of work involved in a position that properly falls within the class
and not in any sense as designating the duties of any position, nor as
affecting or limiting the conceded power with which the employing authority is
now, or hereafter may be, vested with respect to the right to prescribe or
alter the duties of any position; provided, however, that where a substantial
change of duties is made, except for a temporary period or by the addition of
duties that are incidental to the main employment, such changes should be
reported to the Civil Service Commission with a view to a possible
reclassification of the position.
      2.    The "Typical Tasks" shall be construed as examples only,
illustrative of the duties as outlined by the general statement. These examples
are not intended to be complete or exclusive, and the fact that the actual
tasks performed in a position do not apply herein shall not be taken to mean
that the position is necessarily excluded from the class, provided that the
tasks constituting the main work or employment are duly covered by the general
statement of duties. On the other hand, any one example of a typical task,
taken without relationship to the general statement of duties and all other
parts of the specifications, shall not be construed as determining that a
position shall be included within the class.
      3.    The "Minimum Entrance Qualifications" constitute a part of the
description or definition of the kind of employment, by expressing the minimum
qualifications desirable in the case of any new appointee, if he is to perform
the work properly, and is to be so construed as not imposing in itself any new
or additional requirements for the filling of positions. Although they may not
be mentioned in the statement, such qualifications as should apply in common to
all or many positions such as citizenship, suitable age, honesty, sobriety, and
industry, are taken for granted.
Section 8
   For the purpose of assisting in its work in connection with the
classification or reclassification of positions, the Commission may require the
appearance of the appointing authority and the submission of information and
data to support the testimony of such appointing authority in connection with
the classification or reclassification issue then before the Commission.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
RULE III
APPLICATION AND APPLICANT
Section 1
   Every applicant for admission to examination for a position in the
Classified Service:
   A.   Must be a citizen of the United States.
   B.   Must be a resident of the State of Ohio, at date of hire.
   C.   Must present his naturalization papers for inspection at the time he
files his application if not a naturalized citizen.
   D.   Applicants for appointment to the Police Department must be between
ages twenty-one years and thirty-five years at the time of application;
however, the Commission may modify such minimum age requirements in specific
cases and when it may appear reasonable and advisable to do so.
   E.   Applicants for appointments to the Fire Department must be between the
ages of twenty-one years and 35 years at the time of application; however the
Commission may modify such age requirements in specific cases and when it may
appear reasonable and advisable to do so.
   F.   Fire Department applicants must submit proof of enrollment in a
paramedic program at time of exam and must submit a current, valid paramedic
license at time of appointment.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11; Res. 2015-1. Passed 3-10-15; Res. 2017-1. Passed
3-21-17.)
Section 2
   Application for examination must be made in writing upon forms prescribed by
the Commission, signed by the applicant, and sworn to or affirmed before an
officer authorized to administer oaths. The application must be filed by the
applicant or the applicant’s representative at the City Hall within the time
frame set by the Commission. A filing fee, set by the Civil Service Commission,
shall be paid by all persons filing an application for examination.
(Ord. 1996-19. Passed 3-25-96; Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 3
   The applicant must furnish satisfactory proof that he is a person of good
moral character, of correct and orderly deportment, and of temperate and
industrious habits by certificates of no less than two reputable citizens of
the State of Ohio not holding any public office or position in a political
party organization, each certifying that he has been personally acquainted with
the applicant for at least one year and believes him to be of good moral
character, of temperate and industrious habits and in all respects qualified
for the service he desires to enter and that each such citizen is willing that
his certificate shall be made public. Additional certificates of character may
be required in any case in the discretion of the Commission.
Section 4
   No applicant shall be examined, certified as eligible or appointed to any
office in the public service who is found to lack any of the established
preliminary requirements for the examination, who is found to be physically
unfit for the performance of the duties of the position he seeks, who is
addicted to intoxicating liquors or drugs, who has been convicted of a felony,
who has been found guilty of any crime or of infamous or notoriously
disgraceful conduct, who has been dismissed from any branch of the public
service for delinquency or misconduct, or who has made false statements of any
material fact, or practiced or attempted to practice any deception or fraud in
his application or in his examination, or in establishing his eligibility or in
securing his appointments.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 5
   All persons applying for examination for any position, the duties of which
require examination by and the certificate of any board of examiners authorized
under the laws of Ohio, shall present for inspection by the Commission at the
time when he files his application for examination, his certificate from such
board of examiners or a duly certified copy thereof.
Section 6
   The Commission may in its discretion require applicants to furnish a sworn
written statement of their experience qualifying them for the position which
they seek, in which event experience may be regarded as one of the parts of the
examination and a definite weight to be determined by the Commission allotted
thereto.
RULE IV
EXAMINATIONS
Section 1
   Examinations shall consist of one or more tests in any combination. Tests
may be written, oral, physical, demonstration of skill, assessment centers,
work simulations, or an evaluation of training and experiences and shall be
designed to fairly test the relative capacity of the persons examined to
discharge the particular duties of the position for which appointment is
sought.
(Res. 2009-1. Passed 3-11-09.)
Section 2
   Whenever it appears to the Commission that the good of the service will be
promoted thereby, it may have an examination for any office or position in the
Classified Service. Public notice of the time and place of every examination
shall be given at least thirty days prior to the date thereof and posted in
conspicuous public places in the City Hall. When greater publicity shall be
deemed necessary, notice of the examination may also be published in other
marketing/social media outlets. Such notice shall also contain any other
information relating to the scope of the examination, the weights to be
attached to the respective subject and the qualifications of the applicants, as
the Commission may deem proper.
(Res. 2009-1. Passed 3-11-09; Res. 2015-1. Passed 3-10-15.)
Section 3
   Examinations shall be conducted by a special examiner under supervision of
the Commission, and when necessary and advisable so to do special examiners may
be designated to assist in the conduct of the same. Oral interviews may be
required of applicants for positions where personal qualifications are to be
determined, and physical and medical examinations may be required when the
Commission deems it advisable. The report of such physical or medical
examination shall be filed together with the other examination papers with the
Commission.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 4
   The examination shall commence by requiring each applicant to fill out and
sign an identification and declaration sheet containing the examination number
as shown on the official envelope furnished him, also his social security
number and such other information as the Commission may require and the same
shall be sealed in the official envelope. The envelope shall be placed in a
sealed package and deposited in a safe depository and shall be opened for the
identification of papers only after the markings have been completed on all
papers. All examination papers submitted by applicants shall contain their
identification number only.No other identification marks should appear on the
examination paper.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 5
   All markings shall be in accordance with the weights for the respective
subjects established by the Commission and the special examiner. The
examination shall be rated on the scale of 100% for the maximum possible
attainment and 70% for the required passing grade, and shall be ascertained in
accordance with the table of weights for such subjects as fixed by the
Commission and shall be based on approved examination methods. The following
percentages shall be added to a passing grade of 70% (or higher):
   A.   5% if the candidate is a full-time City of Mayfield Heights employee.
   B.   3% if the candidate is a part-time City of Mayfield Heights employee or
an auxiliary or seasonal worker.
   C.   3% for a Fire Department entrance exam candidate who submits
documentation of graduating, in good standing, with a bachelor's degree in fire
sciences or public safety from an accredited institution of higher learning.
   D.   3% for a Police Department entrance exam candidate who submits
documentation of graduating, in good standing, with a bachelor's degree from an
accredited institution of higher learning.
   E.   2% for a Fire Department entrance exam candidate who submits
documentation of graduating, in good standing, with an associate's degree in
fire sciences or public safety from an accredited institution of higher
learning.
   F.   2% for any military person who has been honorably discharged or
transferred to the reserve with evidence of satisfactory service, and submits
an active military ID or a DD214 document with honorable discharge.
   Credit is given for only one degree per candidate. Any extra credit given is
not to exceed 5%.
(Ord. 1996-19. Passed 3-25-96; Res. 2009-1. Passed 3-11-09; Res. 2011-1. Passed
6-2-11; Res. 2015-1. Passed 3-10-15.)
Section 6
   Commencing with the day following the administration of the written portion
of a promotional examination, the questions and answers thereto which the
Commission proposes to use in grading the examination shall be available to
candidates in such examinations in the office of the Commission for a period of
five working days. During this five day period any candidate who desires to
challenge any answer contained in the tentative answer key shall submit such
challenge in writing together with authoritative proof of his or her claim. All
such written challenges shall be considered by the Commission provided,
however, that the identity of the candidates submitting the challenge shall not
be known to the Commission. If the Commission is satisfied as to the validity
of such proposed changes and/or amendments they shall be made part of the
examination answer key. The original examination answer key together with any
changes and/or amendments thereto authorized by the Commission shall constitute
the final examination answer key. No further requests for changes and/or
amendments to the examination answer key shall be entertained by the
Commission. Only the final examination answer key shall be used in scoring all
examination papers.
   Any candidate shall have the right to review his or her own graded
examination papers and to submit written requests for the correction of
clerical errors in their grading during five working days following the
applicant’s notification by mail of his or her grade. The five day period shall
be considered to begin on the day following the day on which such notices are
placed in the United States Mail by the Commission. Thereafter, no candidate
may be permitted to examine his or her graded examination papers or to submit a
request for change in the grading thereof. Examination papers are not subject
to inspection by the public.
(Res. 2009-1. Passed 3-11-09; Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: There is no Section 7 in these Civil Service Rules and
Regulations.)
Section 8
   (A)    Open positions, prospective or otherwise, shall be filled by
promotions whenever practicable. An advancement in rank or an increase in
salary beyond the limit prescribed for the grade shall constitute promotion.
   (B)    Promotions in the Police or Fire Department shall be governed by the
specific rules adopted by the Commission for such Departments. (See Section 9,
Rule IV)
   (C)    Whenever there is a prospective opening in a position in any
department above the lowest grade, the Commission shall ascertain whether there
are at least two employees who have served one year or more in the next lower
grade who are eligible and willing to compete to fill the position. If it is
found that there are at least two such employees the position shall be filled
from an eligible list established by a competitive examination for promotion of
such employees.
   (D)   Whenever there are less than two employees in the next lower grade who
are eligible and willing to compete, the Commission may hold an original
competitive examination to fill the position or, if an eligible list is
available from which to certify such position, the Commission may certify
therefrom or may permit the appointing authority to nominate the employee in
the next lower grade for promotion without competition. In all cases of
promotion without competition, however, the appointing authority shall submit a
written statement showing that the duties performed by the employees nominated
are a natural preparation for the higher position and that such employee is
entitled to promotion by reason of length of experience and effective
performance.
   (E)   If the position to be filled is in the higher grades the Commission
may, if it finds, on account of the executive ability required to fill the
position, that promotion by competitive examination is impractical and not in
the best interest of the service, hold all original competitive examinations
without regard to the number of eligible employees in the next lower grade.
   (F)   In promotional examinations, efficiency and seniority in service shall
form a part of the maximum marks attainable. The Commission may prescribe forms
on which shall be recorded continuous and comparative records of the work and
conduct of all employees in any department for reference by the Commission in
holding a promotional examination or in considering a nomination for promotion
without examination. Credit for seniority shall be given and determined as of
the time of notice of the particular examination in question. Such records
shall at all times be subject to revision by the Commission.
   (G)   The weight to be given for efficiency in any promotional examination
shall be fixed by the Commission at the time notice of the examination is
given. When efficiency records covering the employee eligible for promotion do
not exist, the Commission shall investigate the work and conduct of such
employee and allow such efficiency ratings as it may deem proper.
   (H)    This section has been deleted because it is in conflict with Rule 4,
Section 9(A).
   (I)   Except as otherwise provided herein, the rules and regulations of the
Commission providing for original examinations and the manner of giving notice
thereof shall in general apply to promotional examinations, provided, however,
that no extra credits shall be given for residence or for army or navy service.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 9
   (A)    No position above the grade or rank of patrolman or regular fireman
shall be filled by original appointment.
   (B)    Openings, prospective and otherwise in positions above the rank or
grade of patrolman or regular fireman shall be filled by promotion from among
employees holding positions in a grade or rank lower than the position to be
filled and appointment to such position shall be limited to members of the
respective departments.
   (C)   No position above the rank or grade of patrolman and fireman shall be
filled by any person unless he shall have first passed a competitive
promotional examination to be held by the Commission within sixty days of such
prospective opening, if there is no eligible list for such grade or rank. No
competitive promotional examination shall be held unless there are at least two
persons eligible to complete.
   (D)    Promotions shall be by successive grades or ranks so far as
practicable.
   (E)   No person shall be promoted to a higher rank or grade who has not
served at least twelve months in the next lower grade or rank.
   (F)    When the Commission determines that there are less than two persons
eligible and willing to compete, the Commission shall allow persons in the next
lower rank or grade, who are eligible, to compete with persons in the rank or
grade lower than the position to be filled.
   (G)   All examinations for promotions shall be competitive and may be
conducted in the same manner as examinations described in Ohio R.C. 124.30 and
shall relate to those matters which test the ability of the person to discharge
the particular duties of the position sought. In the case of each examination
the parts or subjects into which it shall be divided and the weight to be
assigned to each part will be determined by the Commission. Credit for
seniority shall be given in accordance with Ohio R.C. 124.31. Also, credit for
efficiency, e.g. performance ratings, may be given as an added credit in
accordance with Ohio R.C. 124.31. No applicant will be accepted to take a
promotional examination while criminal and/or civil charges or complaints are
pending against an applicant.
   (H)   (EDITOR'S NOTE: This paragraph was repealed as part of the 2000
updating and revision of these Codified Ordinances because the provisions
contained therein were superseded by provisions contained in the most recent
collective bargaining contracts with representatives of Division of Police
personnel.)
   (I)    After such promotional examination has been completed, the Commission
shall certify to the appointing authority the names of the three candidates
standing highest on the eligibility list. The Mayor shall appoint one of the
three persons certified to him to the position within thirty days of such
certification.
   (J)   If there is an eligible list, the Commission shall certify to the
appointing authority the names of the three candidates standing highest on the
eligible list and the Mayor shall appoint one of the three persons certified to
him to the position within thirty days of such certification. If less than
three names appear on the eligibility list, only those names shall be
certified.
   (J1)   In promotions in the Police and Fire Departments, credits for
seniority shall be established according to Ohio R.C. 124.31.
(Res. 2009-1. Passed 3-11-09; Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 9A
   In promotions in the Police and Fire Departments, credits for seniority
shall be given as prescribed by Ohio Civil Service Laws, Chapter 124, Section
45, as well as Ohio R.C. 124.45 as follows:
   In promotional examinations, seniority in service shall be added to the
examination grade, but no credit for seniority to an examination grade unless
the applicant achieves at least the minimum passing score on the examination
without counting such extra credit. Credit for seniority shall equal, for the
first four years of service, 1% of the total grade attainable in the promotion
examination, and for each of the fifth through fourteenth years of service,
0.6% of the total grade attainable.
(Res. 2009-1. Passed 3-11-09.)
Section 10
   Any examination may be postponed or cancelled by order of the Commission for
good and sufficient reasons, and such postponements and cancellation shall be
recorded in the minutes of the Commission, together with the reasons therefor.
Section 11
   Any competitor in an examination who is found to be using unfair, unethical
or fraudulent methods in the course of his examination, shall be immediately
dismissed from such examination by the Commission or Examiner. All papers and/
or other testing materials shall be taken up by the Commission or Examiner and
marked void. A report of such action shall be made to the Commission. Such
competitor shall be barred from any future examinations and will be subject to
disciplinary action by the appointing authority.
(Res. 2009-1. Passed 3-11-09.)
RULE V
ELIGIBLE LIST
Section 1
   The names of all candidates who receive a final average of 70% or over on
the examination and are otherwise eligible shall be placed on the appropriate
list in the order of their standing in the examination, and against each name
shall be noted the date of the examination, the date on which the name was
entered on the list, and the average rating.
Section 2
   When two or more eligible candidates have received the same average rating,
the person with the highest random number, received at the time of the written
exam, shall have priority.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 3
   An eligible list shall remain effective for not more than one year except
when otherwise deemed advisable. The Commission may in its discretion, prior to
the date of expiration of eligibility, extend the period of eligibility for any
position or group, provided the total period of eligibility shall not exceed
two years.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 4
   If at any time after the creation of an eligible list the Commission has
reason to believe that any person whose name appears on such list has in any
manner become disqualified for appointment, such person shall be notified and
given opportunity to be heard. If such person shall fail to appear for hearing,
or upon his being heard fails to satisfy the Commission, his name shall be
removed from such eligible list. The hearing must be requested within thirty
days after receipt of notice to disqualify a person from the eligible list. The
hearing will take place within fourteen days after receipt of the request for
hearing, and a decision will be rendered within fourteen days after the hearing
takes place.
RULE VI
REQUISITION CERTIFICATION AND APPOINTMENT
Section 1
   Upon receipt of a written request from the Mayor for certification in the
classified service, the Commission shall review the list to ensure candidates
are still interested in a position and then request fingerprinting and
background checks for the twenty persons standing highest on the appropriate
eligibility list. Upon receipt and review of the results of the background
checks, the Commission shall determine which applicants meet the qualifications
for certification. This process shall continue until the Commission has twenty
qualified applicants standing highest on the appropriate eligible list, at
which time it shall certify the names, addresses and grades of said qualified
applicants to the Mayor. The Mayor shall thereupon appoint one of twenty so
certified to fill the position. Should there be more than one position to be
filled, additional names shall be certified so that at least twice more
eligibles than positions to be filled shall be certified.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11; Res. 2015-1. Passed 3-10-15.)
Section 2
   If an appropriate eligible list contains less than twenty names, the names
remaining on said list may be certified, and the Mayor may appoint from this
certification, or if the circumstances warrant, the Mayor may request a
complete list of ten names.
(Res. 1996-1. Passed 10-18-96; Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11; Res. 2015-1. Passed
3-10-15.)
Section 3
   Such notification for certification shall state the title of the prospective
open position and the department in which the prospective opening exists.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
Section 4
   The person selected for appointment shall be duly notified by the Mayor and
if the person so selected shall fail to report to the appointing authority
within three days from date of such notice, he may be considered as declining
the appointment and his name may be stricken from the eligible list. Another
eligible candidate may then be appointed and be notified of his selection.
Section 5
   The Mayor shall report, within ninety days after certification of names for
appointment or promotion, to the Commission the name of the person appointed or
promoted. The names of those certified and not selected shall be restored to
their respective positions upon the eligible list.
(Res. 2015-1. Passed 5-10-15.)
Section 6
   The person appointed to the position shall be placed on a probationary
period. The probationary period shall be eighteen months, unless otherwise
governed by a collective bargaining agreement in effect at the time of the
appointment, at which time the terms of the collective bargaining agreement
prevail, and the Commission shall be notified thereof. If the fitness, conduct
and ability of the probationer are satisfactory to the Mayor, the probationer's
retention in the service at the end of such probationary period shall be on a
permanent basis. However, should his conduct capacity or fitness be
unsatisfactory, he may be discharged at any time during such probationary
period with no right of appeal.
(Ord. 1996-19. Passed 3-25-96.)
Section 7
   No name shall be certified more than four times to the Mayor, for the same
position, except on the written request of the Mayor.
(Res. 2015-1. Passed 5-10-15.)
Section 8
   In the judgment of the Mayor, emergency or temporary appointments may be
made when the good of the service or the welfare of the public makes it
necessary. Notice, however, must be given to the Commission with the reasons
for making such provisional appointments and such reasons must be satisfactory
to the Commission. An emergency or temporary appointment may be made, but is
not to continue longer than 120 days, and in no case shall successive emergency
or temporary appointments be made. The period of emergency or temporary service
is not counted as part of the probationary service. Emergency or temporary
service does not affect the persons standing on the eligibility list.
(Res. 2011-1. Passed 6-2-11.)
RULE VlI
TRANSFERS, LAYOFFS AND REINSTATEMENTS
(Ohio Revised Code 124.32)
Section 1
   With the consent of the Commission, an employee in the classified service
may be transferred to a similar position in another department having the same
pay and similar duties.
Section 2
   A transfer of an employee from a position in one class to a position in a
higher class with a higher rate of compensation or with different or more
responsible duties, shall be regarded as a promotion and shall be subject to
the rules governing promotions.
Section 3
   If for any reason it becomes necessary to lay off employees in the
classified service, those persons who have been appointed last shall be the
first to be laid off. But the names of such persons to be laid off shall be
returned to their proper positions on the eligible list for recertification and
reappointment whenever conditions necessitating layoffs have been corrected.
Section 4
   The Civil Service Commission shall establish a lay-off list, and the
employees whose names appear on such list shall be first selected to refill the
positions which were subject to the lay-off and which were occupied by the
persons so laid off.
RULE VIII
SUSPENSIONS, REDUCTIONS AND REMOVALS
Section 1
   The tenure of every employee in the classified service shall be during good
behavior and efficient service. No person shall be reduced in pay or position,
laid off, suspended, discharged or otherwise discriminated against by the Mayor
except as hereinafter provided.
Section 2
   For the purpose of discipline, the Mayor may suspend, without pay, any
employee for not exceeding thirty days, provided, however, that continuous
successive suspensions shall not be allowed. A written report of any such
suspension, the period thereof, and reasons therefor, shall be filed with the
Commission within five days.
Section 3
   For inefficiency, dishonesty, drunkenness, incompetency, immoral conduct,
insubordination, discourteous treatment of the public, neglect of duty,
violation of any provisions of the Civil Service Laws of Ohio or the rules and
regulations of this Commission or the Police or Fire Department, or any other
failure of good behavior, or any act of malfeasance, misfeasance or nonfeasance
in office, an employee may be reduced in pay or position, suspended, discharged
or otherwise discriminated against by the Mayor.
Section 4
   (A)    In all cases of suspension, reductions and removal, the Mayor shall
furnish such employee with a copy of the order of suspension, reduction or
removal and his reason for same, and give such employee a reasonable time in
which to make and file an explanation. Such order with the explanation, if any,
must be filed with this Commission.
   (B)    Any such employee in the classified service who is so reduced or
suspended for a period of more than five days, or removed or discharged, or
otherwise discriminated against by the Mayor may appeal to the Civil Service
Commission within ten days, from and after the effective date of such
reduction, suspension or removal.
   (C)    Any such appeal shall be made by filing with the Commission within
said time a written statement of the appeal from such order.
   (D)    The Commission shall notify the Mayor in such an event and shall hear
such appeal within thirty days from and after its filing with the Commission,
giving the appellant and the Mayor not less than five days written notice of
the time and place thereof.
Section 5
   On the hearing of an appeal the Commission shall confine its consideration
to the charges set forth in the order of the Mayor, as filed with the
Commission, and no substantial amendment of nor addition to the said charges
will be permitted or considered by the Commission. The hearings and order of
procedure shall be as follows:
   (A)    The Mayor shall state the grounds and facts alleged to sustain the
order.
   (B)    The appellant shall state his explanation of defense.
   (C)    The Mayor shall present the evidence in support of the order.
   (D)    The appellant shall present the evidence in support of his
explanation or defense.
   (E)    The Mayor shall present any rebuttal evidence.
   (F)    Arguments will be permitted only when desired by the Commission.
Section 6
   The admission and exclusion of evidence, and the determination and decision
of the appeal, shall be governed in general by rules of evidence and burden of
proof applied by the courts in civil cases. Either party may personally
represent himself or be represented by counsel. The Commission shall after due
consideration, render its judgment, affirming, disaffirming or modifying the
order which was the subject of the appeal. In case said judgment is one of
disaffirmance or modification, the appellant shall be reinstated under such
conditions as the Commission may make in connection therewith.
Section 7
   If the appellant shall fail to appear at the time and place set by the
Commission for the hearing of the appeal, appeal may be dismissed by the
Commission. If the Mayor shall fail to appear at such designated time and place
and offer evidence in support of his charges, the Commission may hear evidence
offered by the appellant and render its decision on the merits.
Section 8
   The acceptance by the Mayor of the resignation of any such appellant before
final action on the appeal by the Commission will be considered as a withdrawal
of the charges, and thereupon the appeal shall be dismissed without decision
and the action of the employee thus resigning shall be entered as a
resignation.
RULE IX
LEAVE OF ABSENCE
Section 1
   Leaves of absence without pay may be granted by the Mayor for a period not
to exceed thirty days without the consent of the Commission. Leaves of absence
for a longer period than thirty days shall be granted by the Mayor only with
the consent of the Commission. Written notice of all leaves of absence granted
stating the commencement and period thereof shall be given to the Commission at
once.
RULE X
EFFICIENCY RECORDS
Section 1
   The Mayor or the Director of Public Safety shall make reports, on the forms
furnished by the Commission, on the general conduct of employees, together with
the efficiency and conduct of employees, in the classified service, to the end
that these records may be taken into consideration in promotional examinations
and to promote the general efficiency of the service.
RULE XI
WAIVER OF RULES
Section 1
   Where, in the judgment of the Commission, it is in the interest of the
public service, any of the rules hereby adopted may be waived by a majority
vote of the Commission. Such action and the reasons therefor shall be entered
in the minutes of the meeting of the Commission; in the interest of justice to
all concerned and to promote the welfare of the Civil Service in Mayfield
Heights, a wide degree of liberality of construction and interpretation of
these rules and regulations, in any and all circumstances and situations, shall
be the policy, to be adopted and followed by the Civil Service Commission, in
its administration of the merit system.
RULE XII
AMENDMENTS
Section 1
   The Commission may, in its discretion, change, amend, modify or revoke these
rules or any rule herein, or any part thereof, by a majority vote of the
Commission. One weeks notice of such proposed change together with the text of
the proposal shall be posted in the four most public places selected by the
Commission.
RULE XIII
PRESENT EMPLOYEES
Section 1
   In accordance with the provisions set forth in the Mayfield Heights City
Charter, Article 5, Section 7, each and every person occupying positions or
offices in the classified service of the City of Mayfield Heights, Ohio, as of
January 1, 1952, may be inducted into the Civil Service without examination,
but such positions and offices occupied by them are hereby declared to be
hereafter under the control and supervision of the Civil Service Commission and
under these Rules and Regulations.
RULE XIV
SAVING CLAUSE
Section 1
   If any section or part of a section of these Rules and Regulations is held
by any court to be invalid or unconstitutional, the same shall not invalidate
or impair the validity, force and effect of any other section or part of a
section of these Rules and Regulations, unless it clearly appears that such
other section or part of a section is wholly or necessarily dependent for its
operation upon the section or part of a section held invalid or
unconstitutional.
CHAPTER 169

169.01 ESTABLISHMENT; COMPOSITION.
   There is hereby established in and for the City a Recreation and Parks
Commission. The Commission shall consist of eleven members, two of whom shall
be members of the Committee on Recreation and Parks of Council. The remaining
nine members shall be electors of the City not holding other office,
appointment or employment in the government of the City and shall be appointed
by the Mayor.
(Ord. 1975-6. Passed 2-24-75; Ord. 2016-5. Passed 2-8-16; Ord. 2019-1. Passed
1-28-19; Ord. 2024-20. Passed 10-14-24.)
169.02 TERMS OF OFFICE; VACANCIES.
   The two Council members of the Recreation and Parks Commission shall be
appointed by the President of Council every two years. The other nine members
shall be appointed for a period of five years after their initial appointment,
except that effective March 1, 1975, two shall be appointed for a term of one
year, two for a term of two years, one for a term of three years, one for a
term of four years, one for a term of five years, and beginning January 1,
2025, two additional members shall be appointed for a term of five years each.
A vacancy occurring during the term of any member of the Commission shall be
filled for the unexpired term in the manner authorized for an original
appointment. Consideration should be given in making these appointments to
include electors representing the interests of elementary and secondary school-
age youth, as well as electors representing the interests of senior citizens.
(Ord. 1976-8. Passed 4-12-76; Ord. 2016-5. Passed 2-8-16; Ord. 2019-1. Passed
1-28-19; Ord. 2024-20. Passed 10-14-24.)
169.03 ELECTION OF OFFICERS.
   An organizational meeting shall be held in January of each of the even-
numbered years, at which time a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and such other
officers as may be necessary shall be elected for a period of two years.
(Ord. 1975-6. Passed 2-24-75; Ord. 2019-1. Passed 1-28-19.)
169.04 MEETINGS; RULES AND REGULATIONS; QUORUM; VACANCY.
   The Recreation and Parks Commission shall hold regular meetings and shall
designate the time and place thereof; shall have the power to adopt rules and
regulations for the conduct of business within its jurisdiction; and shall keep
a record of all its proceedings. Five members shall constitute a quorum. A
vacancy in the Commission shall occur when any member fails to be present at
four consecutive meetings or twenty-five percent of the meetings in any fiscal
year, unless such absence is excused by the Commission and the reason therefor
entered in the proceedings.
(Ord. 1975-6. Passed 2-24-75; Ord. 2019-1. Passed 1-28-19.)
169.05 BUDGET.
   The Recreation and Parks Commission shall submit to the Mayor an estimate of
anticipated revenues and expenditures for the coming fiscal year, to be
approved in whole or in part by Council and included in the budget on or before
June 1 of each year. The Commission shall operate within the budget as approved
and the expenses of the City's outdoor swimming pool shall not be included in
this budget.
(Ord. 1975-6. Passed 2-24-75; Ord. 2019-1. Passed 1-28-19.)
169.06 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   The Recreation and Parks Commission shall:
   (a)   Plan, organize and establish policies to provide, within the
limitation of available funds, a year-round recreation and leisure time program
for all residents;
   (b)   Make recommendations to the Mayor and Council concerning the nature,
function, use, utilization, maintenance, beautification, control and regulation
of parks; the acquisition of additional park land; the sale or other alienation
of all or part of any park; and the development, program and operations of
playgrounds, parks and other recreational facilities of the City;
   (c)   Recommend to the Director of Recreation and Parks annually all fees
and charges for participation in the various activities and programs within the
Commission's operational jurisdiction; and
   (d)   Assist organized groups conducting recreation and leisure time
activities and programs and appoint such citizen committees as the Commission
deems necessary.
   (e)   Coordinate with a five member senior subcommittee, appointed bi-
annually by the Mayor, to implement programs and services for the City’s senior
adults.
(Ord. 1975-6. Passed 2-24-75; Ord. 2016-5. Passed 2-8-16; Ord. 2019-1. Passed
1-28-19.)
169.07 GIFTS AND BEQUESTS.
   The Recreation and Parks Commission may solicit and receive gifts, bequests,
other personal property or donations, either the principal or income of which
is to be used for Municipal and/or park purposes.
(Ord. 1975-6. Passed 2-24-75; Ord. 2019-1. Passed 1-28-19.)

CHAPTER 175
Keep Mayfield Heights Beautiful Commission
175.01   Establishment; composition; compensation of members.
175.02   Officers; procedures.
175.03   Program; guidelines; budget; other duties.
175.01 ESTABLISHMENT; COMPOSITION; COMPENSATION OF MEMBERS.
   (a)   There is hereby established the Keep Mayfield Heights Beautiful
Commission in and for the City, which shall be an affiliate of Keep America
Beautiful, Inc., a national non-profit agency. The Commission shall consist of
five members appointed by the Mayor and confirmed by Council, all of whom shall
be electors in the City but not a member of any other board or commission of
the City. The term of office shall be five years, with the term of the first
Commission member appointed to expire on December 31, 2018, and one each
December 31 thereafter.
   (b)   In addition to the appointed members of the Commission, one member of
Council, who shall be appointed by the President of Council, the Director of
Public Service and the Director of Recreation and Parks shall be ex-officio
members and shall meet with and advise the Commission but shall not have the
right to vote. The Director of Public Service shall be the Executive Director
of the Commission.
   (c)   Members of the Commission shall serve without remuneration, other than
the regular salary, if any, provided for the City officials and employees who
are ex-officio members.
(Ord. 2017-18. Passed 10-23-17.)
175.02 OFFICERS; PROCEDURES.
   (a)   The officers of the Keep Mayfield Heights Beautiful Commission shall
be a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and a Secretary, who shall be elected annually
by the Commission from its membership.
   (b)   The Commission may adopt rules of procedure and shall establish a
schedule of regular quarterly meetings. All meetings shall be open to the
public, which shall have the right to address the Commission.
(Ord. 2017-18. Passed 10-23-17.)
175.03 PROGRAM; GUIDELINES; BUDGET; OTHER DUTIES.
   (a)   The program of the Keep Mayfield Heights Beautiful Commission is to
study, formulate and develop plans to reduce litter by identifying the sources
and changing littering behavior; to encourage recycling; to promote public
interest in the beautification and improvement of public and private areas; and
to instill an interest in beautification of residential and commercial
properties in the City.
   (b)   The Commission shall be authorized to propose new ordinances and to
make recommendations for amendments to the Codified Ordinances of the City that
may, directly or indirectly, have an impact on the Commission's purposes.
   (c)   The Commission shall have the power to promote public awareness of the
importance of recycling to the City, including the authority to plan and
publicize recycling programs.
   (d)   The Commission shall prepare a budget for the funds the City may
designate or receive to implement its plans in the streets of, and on public
property owned by, the City.
   (e)   The Commission may publish and distribute pertinent educational
materials to residents of the City. Any costs incurred by such an effort are
subject to approval by Council.
(Ord. 2017-18. Passed 10-23-17.)

CHAPTER 191
Lyndhurst Municipal Court
   EDITOR'S NOTE: The Lyndhurst Municipal Court is established by Ohio R.C.
1901.01. Ohio R.C. 1901.02 provides that the Court has territorial jurisdiction
within the corporate limits of the Municipalities of Highland Heights, Mayfield
Heights, Gates Mills, Mayfield and Richmond Heights in Cuyahoga County. The
powers, duties and proceedings of the Court are established by Ohio R.C.
Chapter 1901. Ohio R.C. 1901.25 provides that the Municipal Court may provide
by rule how jurors shall be chosen. Jurors' fees in any criminal case involving
the violation of a City ordinance shall be paid out of the City Treasury. The
Municipal Court, pursuant to Ohio R.C. 1901.26(A), may establish a schedule of
fees and costs to be taxed in any action or proceeding, whether civil or
criminal. Rule 13 of the Ohio Traffic Rules provides that all courts, other
than juvenile courts, must establish a Traffic Violations Bureau and specifies
certain restrictions as to the designated offenses and schedule of fines to be
accepted as waiver payment in lieu of court appearance.
